profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, and traded under the ticker CRNC. Its site describes it as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, and as providing what it calls the trusted interaction and action layer for physical AI. The company says its platform combines voice, multimodal understanding, contextual intelligence, agentic architecture, and governed execution to help people communicate and collaborate with vehicles, machines, and other intelligent systems.

The site names Cerence xUI, which it says combines speech, vision, and vehicle data to understand driver intent and deliver context-aware in-car experiences, and Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection (EVD), an audio AI system that detects and localizes more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries. Cerence says EVD can identify approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away using interior microphones and beyond 800 meters when paired with exterior microphones, and that it is already deployed in production vehicles. The site also describes work with Microsoft on Zero Trust architecture for in-car assistants, and a demo by Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich on speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments. Cerence reports third quarter results with revenue up 12% YoY, connected services revenue up 20% YoY, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program.

The company's SEC CIK is 0001768267. No lawsuits involving Cerence are recorded, and its litigation exposure is concentrated in Massachusetts, with a count of 191.
